newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold prices sink, volume remains high.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold prices sink, volume remains high.

text.p: Traded volume on the Istanbul gold exchange eased from Tuesday's 1,225 kg, but remained unseasonably high at 990 kg on Wednesday with banks engaging in arbitrage deals for the third consecutive day, dealers said.

Gold's dollar price sank to $351.00 an ounce at Wednesday's close from Tuesday's $354.50 in line with falling worldwide values. Lira values also eased to 1,298,000 lira per gramme versus the previous 1,303,200 despite the lira's sharp decline against the dollar.
The Turkish lira dropped to 115,000 to the dollar from 114,150 at Tuesday's close.
Falling gold prices and the rising dollar enabled banks to make arbitrage deals by buying gold in dollars and selling in lira, which accounted for the bulk of the day's trade, dealers said.
Of the day's 990 kg of trade, 68.7 percent was in lira terms. The bulk of the trade was done in the morning with 930 kg.
